## Non-negotiable invariants

- Always save and restore clipboard after 500 ms settle.
- Re-verify foreground window before paste; otherwise use insert:fallback.
- Never synthesize Enter.
- Refuse password fields.
- Store secrets only in Windows Credential Manager; never log them.
- Treat <draft> as a data boundary in every system prompt.

## Architecture and control flow

- src-tauri/src/platform: Windows integration, foreground focus, hotkeys, clipboard, selection, windows.
- src-tauri/src/domain: settings, prompts, providers, session storage, logs, device id.
- src/components and src/hooks: React UI and orchestration.
- src/store: Zustand state.
- src/services: provider lanes, prompt hardening, auth/API clients, Tauri bridge.
- Desktop auth: system browser uses Authorization Code + PKCE; insertgo:// callback returns code only; session token stays in OS credential storage.

## Commands

- npm run tauri:dev — full desktop app
- npm run build — TypeScript and Vite build
- npm run test:run — frontend tests once
- cd src-tauri && cargo test — Rust tests
- npm run context:sync — regenerate agent context files

## Working rules

- Prefer small reviewable changes and existing abstractions.
- Keep UI in components/hooks, state in stores/services, platform code in Rust platform modules, domain logic in Rust domain modules.
- Use safe Rust and explicit Result errors. Keep unavoidable unsafe code tiny, documented, and tested.
- Do not invent platform APIs. Document limits before raw Windows calls.
- Validate external input; never log prompts, credentials, tokens, or provider secrets.
- Preserve prompt data-boundary and output-sanitization contracts from SPEC.md section 15.
